fig_the_hole.title: The hole: games demand 30–45° DB breaks the Combine does not test
fig_the_hole.claim: The Combine contains no deliberate 30–45° DB break at speed: the 4 sample detections are incidental fragments, not a test, while games demand 97 such turns.
caveats: Exposure: 122 Combine players × one session vs 33 game players × 299 player-games; the share panel exists because the two settings are not sampled alike.
DB demand denominator is all 2,262 valid DB game turns; the snap-classified COVERAGE subset is 1,111, and 1,121 turns (49.6%) are snapped as "other".
Bands are left-closed; the final class is >180°.

fig_drill_coverage.title: Every DB drill asks for a big turn at low speed — the 30–45° cell is effectively empty
fig_drill_coverage.claim: Of 1,179 valid Combine DB turns across 10 drills, 4 (0.3%) fall in the 30–45° × 2–6 yd/s cell the games demand; the repertoire is big-angle at low entry speed.
caveats: Combine supply is 122 players × one session; the figure describes the test inventory, not player populations.
Median reps per player is 1–2 in every drill; even the best-covered band (60–90°) gives a median of 2.
The target cell holds 4 incidental Combine turns from 3 players; game demand in the 30–45° band is 97 turns from 25 players.

fig_before_after.title: Before and after: a 30–45° hole, and the drill that would fill it
fig_before_after.claim: Measured DB Combine supply is 1,179 turns across 7 × 6 angle × entry-speed cells, with only 4 turn(s) in the 30–45° band; the proposed drill would add 732 projected turns to that band.
caveats: The right panel is arithmetic, not measurement: it repeats the measured supply and adds a hatched projection of 6 reps × 122 DBs.
The 2–6 yd/s window is split by the grid's 4 yd/s edge and the drill spec has no per-cell split, so the total is carried once on the region and never divided between cells.
Exposure: Combine supply is 122 players × one session; the projection is 6 reps per player. Turn counts are not comparable samples of behaviour.
Blank cells are real zeros; the CSV records every grid cell, including empty ones.

omitted_not_specified: Gate width (the opening between gate posts) is not stated in the proposal, so each exit gate is drawn as a single transverse tick marking where the player crosses — not as a measured opening.
The proposal lists exactly two approach cones 8-10 yd apart and puts the break cone at the end of the approach; it does not describe any further cone. Only those two cones are drawn.

Where the walk-in ends and where the 2-yd run-up sits relative to the 8-10 yd approach is not specified, so no phase boundary is drawn: the phases are labelled in one line, and only the approach itself (8-10 yd) is measured on the image.
The 3-cone footprint the new drill reuses is not dimensioned in the proposal, so no footprint outline is drawn — the claim is stated in words only.
Lane width, station size and cone spacing beyond the two approach cones are not specified and are not drawn.

fig_all_positions.title: The same hole across positions: 30–45° breaks are rare in the Combine and common in games
fig_all_positions.claim: Every panel plots the same quantity — the share of that setting's own valid turns in each 30–45° reporting band, Combine vs game, on one identical 0–70% axis. What each panel shows differs by position (DL: 34 vs 25 turns in 30–45°); the figure ranks no position and labels no panel "fine".
fig_all_positions.position_order_note: Order as TASK.md §1 lists the positions; not a ranking by gap size. No position is ranked or dropped.

shared_axis.metric: share of that setting's own valid turns (percent)

spec_status.source: TASK.md:63 and TASK.md:153 — OL and DB are exploratory (contamination risk); TASK.md:136 the same for the demand map
spec_status.note: Carried from the spec, not assigned here. Positions absent from this map carry no status on this figure and are neither promoted nor demoted.

caveats: Descriptive shares of a census of turns: no confidence bands, no per-position significance test, no ranking of positions by gap size.
Exposure differs by setting and by position (one Combine session vs several player-games per player), which is why each bar is that setting's own share rather than a count.
DB is both the case's focus and marked exploratory in the spec (TASK.md:63, TASK.md:153). Both signals are drawn as specified; the tension is left open for Conor.
DL is included unchanged and is not annotated as "fine": its panel shows no 30–45° shortfall, and TASK.md §CURRENT FOCUS records DL's gap as a speed story rather than an angle one.
Bands are left-closed; the final class is >180°.

fig_measurement_limits.title: The measurement limits: why this data cannot rank players
fig_measurement_limits.claim: 43 of 51 between-player variance components sit at the boundary of the envelope's grid, so a per-player ranking is not supported by this data; and reversal-class turns carry non-physical lateral accelerations, so they are measured as plants rather than as v·ω. The boundary is a finding about the data, not an error, and the detector still recovers planted turns at 3.1° MAE / precision 0.915 / recall 0.931.

boundary.encoding: zero-width empty bar outlined on the baseline with a hollow point; never shortened to a positive bar and never omitted
boundary.meaning: between-player variance at the floor of the grid to the precision this data supports — a limit of the data, not a bug

reversal_zone.reason: reversal-class turns are measured as plants (apex, exit, regain), never as v·ω; their lateral accelerations are not physical capacity

detector_evidence.note: The MAE is the synthetic planted-corner recovery; the precision/recall are the real-schema three-cone gate. They are quoted together as the counterweight to the boundary, not as one combined test.

caveats: AT_BOUNDARY is a finding about the data, not a model failure; it is drawn, counted, and never silently dropped.
No per-player ranking, player names, scores, p-values or error bars on counts appear in this figure.
Lateral acceleration is pooled across settings; the panel describes the physics of turn types, not a setting comparison.
The reversal threshold is configured, not inferred from the plot: figures.measurement_limits.reversal_zone_deg.

fig_gap_honest.title: How big is the gap, really? Raw counts, own-turn share and turns per player-appearance
fig_gap_honest.claim: The 4-vs-97 raw count is a 24.25× ratio inflated by exposure (122 Combine players measured once vs 33 game players over 299 player-games); on each setting's own turns the gap is 4.29% vs 0.34% = 12.6×, and per player-appearance 0.324 vs 0.033 = 9.9× — still damning.
fig_gap_honest.headline_reason: The headline keeps figure 1's population — all valid DB turns, angles >=180 kept as their own class — so the correction describes the same turns as the 4-vs-97 claim it answers.

caveats: The raw count is exposure-confounded: one Combine session per player versus many player-games per game player. Panels b and c divide by each setting's own exposure and are the honest comparison.

not_plotted.reason: exit_speed / entry_speed; the turn window runs between speed maxima, so re-acceleration inside the window makes it exceed 1 by construction. Definitional footnote only, never a cost.

panel_a.shape: The curve is not monotone in angle: Combine rises from 45–60° to 60–90°; Game rises from 30–45° to 45–60° and 45–60° to 60–90°; shallowest to deepest reported band, Combine 1.00 → 0.14; Game 0.82 → 0.28.

reversal_class.in_panel_b: included as a labelled, hatched class

caveats: Sample data: nothing here is a finding about the 2027 class.

apex_retention is apex_speed / entry_speed: the speed lost at the plant. speed_retention (exit / entry) is above 1 by construction because the window runs between speed maxima and includes re-acceleration; it is a definitional footnote, never a cost.
Descriptive only: no per-player values, no ranking, no p-values, no smoothing or fitted curve.
Bands are figures.hole.bands, left-closed; the last class is the reversal class and carries no retention value.

revision.reason: Figure 8 originally plotted speed_retention (exit ÷ entry), which is above 1 in every band by construction and shows gains, not costs. Panel (a) now plots apex_retention (apex ÷ entry), the speed actually given up at the plant.

fig_stopwatch.title: Same stopwatch, different turn: what the published three-cone time compresses

match.rule: nfl_id join to files.combine_results three_cone (not null); turns from outputs/turns/turns.parquet where drill_name contains 'THREE_CONE', setting == 'combine', position_group == 'DB', valid == true

panel_a.encoding: one row per player sorted by published three-cone time, one dot per detected turn on the angle axis; light rules at the reporting band edges only

panel_b.encoding: entry speed of each detected turn against the same published time; min-max line per player; no fit

fig_stopwatch.claim: The published three-cone time is one scalar; the drills behind it contained visibly different turns at different entry speeds, so the metric cannot distinguish them by construction.
not_claimed: That three-cone time fails to predict turn angle or entry speed.
That any difference between players is a difference in ability.
Any correlation, R², regression, p-value or fitted curve.
caveats: Sample data: one session of sample data; nothing here is a finding about the 2027 class.
Descriptive only: the figure shows what the metric compresses, not how well it predicts. With this many matched players an association test would be underpowered, so none is run.
Turns are pooled across attempts within the drill; the attempt count per player is printed in the CSV and stated in the caption.
A player's row is the detector's own valid turns, not a scout's reading of the drill; detection limits apply as in every other figure.

fig_both_hips.title: The test never checks which way he turns

direction.sign_convention: turn_angle = unwrapped heading change over the turn segment, end minus start; heading = atan2(vx, vy) in degrees mod 360, i.e. 0 = +y with the angle increasing clockwise (kinematics.heading_deg). Turning left is therefore a NEGATIVE turn_angle and turning right a POSITIVE one, once it is known which side of a player +y lies on; that is what the checks below decide, not assume.

chirality_check.rule: targeted receiver's tracked side of y = field_mid_y must match the side named in the description, with the mapping flipping between play_direction left and right

families_not_carried.reason: below the 80% floor or n=20 on at least one side: y_above_mid 36/44 (82%); y_below_mid 31/45 (69%)
below the 80% floor or n=20 on at least one side: y_above_mid 23/31 (74%); y_below_mid 28/36 (78%)

orientation_check.field: o (game tracking only; absent in the Combine)
orientation_check.role: supporting only: o shares the heading frame, so it cannot pin handedness by itself

fig_both_hips.claim: The Combine's shallow-turn band is a handful of incidental fragments (median about one turn per player), so the Combine cannot be testing that a defensive back can break both ways, while games demand both directions about evenly.
not_claimed: That any asymmetry exists in these players' bodies or skills.
That a 15/11 split of 26 turns from 16 players is evidence of anything about a body.
Any symmetry test, binomial p-value, confidence interval, correlation or fitted effect for the split.
caveats: Sample data: one session of sample data; nothing here is a finding about the 2027 class.
Descriptive counts only. The split is not tested for symmetry and no p-value is computed anywhere in the figure's code path.
The capacity envelope is fitted on |turn_angle| with no direction term, so it deliberately cannot model a left/right asymmetry; this figure is not a modelled effect.
Direction labels come from the recorded chirality and route checks, not from convention alone; where either fails the bars fall back to SIDE A / SIDE B.
